description.narrative: The approach for the first phase of the new initiative will be focused on set-up activities, including assembling the core team, condcuting research, engaging with member states to identify and develop a portfolio of large-scale transformative bankable projects, and building relationships with prospective private sector investors, working in collaboration with SGO. Once the first tranche of transformative bankable projects have been identified and are ready to approach private sector investors, the next phase of the project will be focused on enabling investments by the private sector. The opportunity for enabling these would be explored during CHOGM 2026 or future economic or business forums, by leveraging on the presence of Heads of State, ministers and Governments to progress flagship deals. The Secretariat's role is to act as a neutral partner working in close collaboration with member state and potential investors, ensuring that Commonwealth principles are respected. The first two years will focus on Africa due to pre-existing networks, whilst also exploring opportunities for small states. Year 3 & 4 will refine the approach (by applying the lessons learnt from Africa) to scale-up opportunities across all regions. Furthermore, by Year 3, it is expected that this new initiative should be self-sustainable by attracting private sector investors to sponsor its running costs. Regular investor roadshows and investor engagements are expected to be organised in London and other financial hubs. Year 4 will focus more on the financing of large infrastructural projects, and the establishment of an M&E framework to track progress. In the longer-term, once financing has been obtained and the transformative project has been materialised, it is expected that intra-Commonwealth trade and investment will increase significantly toward achieving the goal of $2 trillion to 2030.
